headline_campaigns.name: CIPHER (Complement of Integrated Protocols for Human Exploration Research)
headline_campaigns.description: An integrated series of up to 14 physiological and psychological studies conducted on ISS astronauts on short, standard (6-month), and extended (1-year) missions.
core_investigations: Bone mineral density changes and biomechanical strength
Ocular structure alterations and optic nerve sheath dilation (SANS)
Immune system biomarkers and microbiome shifts
Cognitive performance degradation and sleep architecture

headline_campaigns.name: Standard Measures
headline_campaigns.description: A baseline data repository collecting a standardized set of physiological, behavioral, and biochemical data from every ISS astronaut before, during, and after flight.
data_collected: Biochemical: blood chemistry, hematology, urinalysis, endocrine hormones
Physiological: body mass, exercise vitals, ECG, spirometry
Sensorimotor: posture, dynamic balance, gait analysis
Psychological: sleep diary, cognitive test batteries (Cognition test), stress surveys

headline_campaigns.name: Ground-Based Analog Environments
headline_campaigns.description: Earth-based isolated habitats simulating microgravity, isolation, and communication latency to validate countermeasures prior to flight.
facilities: HERA (Human Exploration Research Analog) at NASA Johnson Space Center: 45-day simulated isolation campaigns testing crew dynamics, sleep debt, and autonomous operations.
CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog): 3D-printed Mars habitat evaluating 1-year missions.
:envihab & Bed-Rest Studies: -6 degree head-down tilt bed rest mimicking microgravity cephalad fluid shifts and bone/muscle disuse.
Antarctic Research Stations: long polar winter confinement evaluating extreme cold isolation and circadian disruption.
